# CI Workflows

- `reusable-consumer.yml`: nine checks plus the `dx-ci (aggregate)` gate.
- `reusable-release.yml`: on a tag push, or on any ref when `publish` is false, dry-runs on each `platforms` entry, then applies `dx deploy` for each `deployment` tagged `release` (or the `deployables` input), the `registry_deploys` of a `github_deploy` first, with `contents`, `id-token`, `attestations` and `packages` write. The release job runs only when `publish` is true (the default) and the ref is a tag, so a branch run never publishes. A failure stops the rest and the job summary lists what was published. `dx init` writes a `release.yml` caller.
- `release-e2e.yml`: on a `v0.0.0-e2e.*` tag push, calls `reusable-release.yml` from this repository with the `//tools/testing/release_e2e` fixtures: `a_github` alone, or `a_github` then `b_refuses` when the tag contains `partial`. `b_refuses` keeps the placeholder tag `v0.0.0-dryrun`, so its dry run passes and its publish fails.
- `reusable-docs.yml`: `docs-check` plus `docs-publish` (GitHub Pages).
- `docs.yml`: on a push to `main` that changes a page in the user book (`docs/`, `tools/docs/`, the root and example READMEs), or by dispatch, runs `reusable-docs.yml` and publishes the book to https://devhusdk.github.io/rules_dx/. Its `docs` job and the `ci.yml` `docs` job share the `docs-pages-<ref>` concurrency group, so two Pages deploys never overlap.
- `pr-check.yml`: on pull requests and dispatch, an `analysis` job on `ubuntu-latest` for `producers_bin --pr-check` (`tools/ci/producers/src/pr_check.rs`), one step per set (`workflow`, `preflight`, `starter`, `hermetic`, `docs`, `cli`, `kotlin-bench`) so the run shows each set's duration. `preflight` also runs the `ci.yml` crate lockfile check (#8915). In parallel, `affected-plan` lists the tests `dx test --affected` reaches and splits them into shards of at most 150, and the `affected` matrix runs one shard per job, so neither the sets nor a change that reaches most of the repository push a job past its time budget. Run one locally from the workspace root with `bazel build //tools/ci/producers:producers_bin && bazel-bin/tools/ci/producers/producers_bin --pr-check <set>`. The owner decides whether it moves to `pull_request` or `merge_group` (#7172).
- `api-label.yml`: on pull requests and label changes, fails when the pull request changes a file under `api/` (a rename out of it counts) and has no `api` label. Runs on `ubuntu-slim`.
- `pr-links.yml`: on pull requests, including body edits, runs `producers_bin --pr-links` on the body and commit messages. It also runs on `merge_group`, where it reads the body of the pull request named in the queue ref, and `.github/rulesets/main.json` requires it on main. It fails when the body has no `Closes #N`, `Part of #N` or `No issue: <reason>` line, or when the body or a commit names an issue with a work phrase ("fixes", "part of", "slice", "draft for", "implements", "fixed by this PR") that no `Closes` or `Part of` line links. Replay a body locally with `GITHUB_EVENT_PATH=event.json bazel-bin/tools/ci/producers/producers_bin --pr-links [COMMITS_FILE]`.
- `ci.yml`: this repository's own `ci` gate. A failed Windows preflight build uploads `rmeta-diagnostics-<platform>` (#4850).
- When the `gate` check or the `evidence.yml` test task fails, `producers_bin --test-log-tails` prints the last 80 lines of each failing test's `test.log` in its own `::group::` in the job log, for the first 20 failing tests.
- `ci.yml` jobs `preflight`, `quality-matrix` and `launch-heavy` upload the compact execution log of their test step as `exec-log-<job>-<platform>` for 7 days. To see why spawns missed the cache, download the artifact from two runs and run `bazel run //tools/testing:determinism_check -- diff <first.log> <second.log>`. It prints the 20 slowest remote-cacheable spawns that ran in the second run (`--top N` changes the count), each with the inputs, args and env that differ from the first run, or why it could not hit the cache. Before those lines, up to 5 `origin:` lines follow each differing input back through the spawns that made it, to a changed source file, to a spawn the first run does not have or whose args or env differ, or to a spawn that gave a different output from the same inputs. Last, `not remote cacheable, ran every time:` lists the count and total time of the spawns that cannot be cached, such as test runs, per mnemonic.
- `ci.yml` job `determinism` runs five shards. Each builds a fifth of the top-level packages that hold one target of each `lang.json` entry_points kind, plus `//appimage/...` (shard 0), `//cli/archive/...` (shard 1), `//android/private/packaging/...` (shard 2), `//msix/tests/...` (shard 3) or `//deploy/private/...` (shard 4), twice in fresh output bases with no cache and compares the execution logs against `tools/ci/determinism_allowlist.txt`.
- `ci.yml` job `in-graph-prebuilt-guard` runs `//tools/testing/consumer:in_graph_prebuilt_guard`, which analyzes the `IN_GRAPH_GUARD_LANGS` consumer fixtures of `@dx_api_fixtures` on linux_x86_64, and the `MACOS_IN_GRAPH_GUARD_LANGS` ones with `--langs` on macos_arm64, with `--//cli/prebuilt:guard_view` and the `dx check` and `dx docs` aspects and fails when they compile a rules_dx binary that `tools/testing/consumer/prebuilt_guard_allowlist.txt` does not name.
- `ci.yml` job `analysis-scaling` runs `//tools/testing:analysis_scaling_check`, which analyzes the `//tools/testing/deep_graph` chains of depth 100 and 400 with the `dx check`, `dx docs` and `dx sync` aspects and fails when depth 400 takes more than 8 or less than 2 times depth 100.
- `issue-labels.yml`: daily warning for open issues older than one day, except pinned ones, that have no P0 to P3 label. Writes a job summary. Runs on `ubuntu-slim`.
  A second job warns about labels named in `CONTRIBUTING.md` or issue template front matter that do not exist in the repository (#6643).
- `evidence.yml`: native evidence on hosted runners, dispatched per run. The run posts the commit status `evidence/<platform>/<task>/<scope>` on the dispatched commit: pending at dispatch, then success, failure or error. The `evidence-<platform>` artifact holds `evidence.log` and each test's log, XML and undeclared outputs. Set `platforms` to `["macos_arm64"]` for Apple runs. Set `android` to boot an emulator and run the Rust Android device scenarios on `linux_x86_64`. Set `qualify` on `windows_x86_64` to run `//cc/private/tools/context:qualify` for llvm and msvc. Set `relocate` (test or build). With `task=test` it reruns the task under a fresh `--output_base` with the disk cache off and remote cache hits refused; the second run logs to `relocated.log`, and `bazel-testlogs` then points at the relocated base. With `task=build` it runs `//tools/testing:determinism_check` on `scope`, which builds it twice in fresh output bases with no cache and compares the execution logs against `tools/ci/determinism_allowlist.txt`; its output is `determinism.txt` and it fails on any unlisted difference. Set `lock_refresh` to regenerate `MODULE.bazel.lock` on the platform before the scope task and fail when it differs from the checkout; the refreshed lock and `lock.diff` land in `lock/` of the artifact, so a lock entry that only changes on Windows can be copied back. Set `release_cell` to build and qualify the platform's release cell first with `producers_bin --release-cell`, the command `release-cells.yml` runs, uncached and without RBE; the files land in `release-cell/` of the artifact. A Windows release cell needs `accept_licenses` set to the ids that `windows_accept_licenses` of `release-cells.yml` defaults to.
- `evidence-command.yml`: a comment on an issue or pull request whose first line starts with `/evidence`, from an owner, member or collaborator, dispatches `evidence.yml` and replies with the run URL. On a pull request it runs on the PR branch, otherwise on `main`. Arguments are `platforms=`, `task=`, `scope=`, `test_timeout=`, `displays=`, `android=`, `qualify=`, `relocate=`, `release_cell=`, `flags=`, `lock_refresh=` and `accept_licenses=`, for example `/evidence platforms=["macos_arm64"] task=test scope=//haskell/...`. `evidence.yml` validates them and a rejected run fails there.
- `lock-refresh-command.yml`: a comment on a pull request whose first line is `/lock-refresh`, from an owner, member or collaborator, dispatches `lock-refresh.yml` on the PR branch with `pr` set to that pull request and replies with the run URL. The only argument is `nested=true` or `nested=false` (the default). A pull request from a fork is rejected.
- `dx-update.yml`: weekly `tools/dx update --pr` for dependency updates. `dx init` writes `cli/adopt/templates/dx-update.yml`, the same workflow without the BuildBuddy remote execution steps. Where `lock-refresh.yml` exists, it then dispatches that workflow for each open `dx-update/` branch whose `MODULE.bazel.lock` changes the `rules_python` `python` or `rules_go` `go_sdk` entries.
- `pin-android-maven.yml`: dispatch-only. Runs `REPIN=1 bazel run @rules_android_maven//:pin` on `ubuntu-latest` and uploads `rules_android_maven_install.json` as an artifact to commit after a rules_android or rules_flutter bump, so the lock is not resolved through Coursier on a throttled network (#7184).
- `lock-refresh.yml`: dispatch-only. Runs `bazel mod deps --lockfile_mode=update` on the five platforms, merges them with `producers_bin --lock-merge`, which starts from the `linux_x86_64` lock and replaces each extension's `os:<os>,arch:<arch>` entry whole with the one from that platform's own lock (and deep-merges `facts`); it fails when a platform lock is missing, a directory is not a known platform, or an extension has a key other than `general` or a platform factor, normalises the result with Bazel and uploads the locks as an artifact to commit. Run it with `--ref <branch>` after changing `MODULE.bazel` when an extension is locked per platform; one host only writes its own entries. With `nested` set, it also runs the nested tests in record mode on `linux_x86_64`, `macos_arm64` and `windows_x86_64` and merges their records into `tools/testing/nested_cache` with `nested_cache_update --from`; dispatch it that way after a `bazel_dep` bump. With the `pr` input, the merge job also commits the merged locks and nested cache sets to that pull request's branch, using the dx-update app token, and does nothing when they are unchanged.
- `verify-pins.yml`: weekly `//core/quality/artifacts:update -- --verify-only`. It fails naming each stale record.
- `patch-upstream.yml`: weekly `//patches:upstream`. It reads the `Upstream:` header of each patch under `patches/` and the `# Upstream:` carry markers in `BUILD` and `.bzl` files, and opens, or updates, the issue "patches: upstream fixes released" when an upstream pull request is merged and in a release, a ref was closed without a merge, or a patch has no header.
- `release-cells.yml`: reusable, read-only. Builds, independently rebuilds and qualifies one archive per `//deploy/private/release:release_matrix` cell on its native runner (a consumer Bazel build included), then verifies all records. The `windows_accept_licenses` input (by default the Visual Studio Build Tools licence) lists the licence ids the Windows cells' consumers accept at `dx init`; it is the only place the release names a licence. Artifacts: `release-cell-<name>` per cell and the combined `release-cells`; outputs: `version`, `sha`, `workflow_ref`. It fails when any cell is rejected, and a rejected cell never stops the others.
- `release-tools.yml`: reusable, read-only. Builds the deadnix, selene, topiary and progenitor binaries on `linux-x86_64`, `linux-arm64`, `macos-arm64` and `windows-x86_64` (static musl binaries on Linux), ad-hoc signs the `macos-arm64` ones, builds static kcov on the two Linux hosts as `dx-kcov-<host>`, builds it a second time and compares the two execution logs with `//tools/testing:determinism_check`, and uploads `release-tool-<host>`, holding the binaries, their licences, the deadnix source crate and the kcov source archive. Its `python-tools` job builds the `dx-python-tools-<host>.tar.gz` bundles of the core Python quality tools for every release host on `linux-x86_64` and uploads `release-tool-python-tools`. Its `go` job cross-builds the `dx-go-<host>` Go tool multicall and `dx-oapi-codegen-<host>` for every release host on `linux-x86_64`, checks each binary's format, copies `dx-oapi-codegen-LICENSE`, runs the Linux ones and uploads `release-tool-go`. Its `python-tools`, `go` and `jars` jobs, and the Linux legs of its `tools`, `haskell` and `hackage` jobs, also build their assets twice in fresh output bases with `//tools/testing:determinism_check` and fail when the execution logs differ.
- `release.yml`: calls `release-cells.yml` for the five platform archives and `release-tools.yml` for the tool binaries, builds the `rules_dx-<version>.tar.gz` source archive (after `release_driver` checks the tag against the candidate commit), then attests the manifest and uploads them through `release_driver` with the raw dx and dx gazelle binaries, `.sha256` files, the `dx-sha256sums.txt` and `dx-gazelle-sha256sums.txt` and `dx-tool-sha256sums.txt` manifests, and `source.json` to the release, then runs `dx security --verify` on `dx-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` and the source archive and on a one-byte-modified copy of each. The `dry_run` dispatch input runs the same `source`, `attest` and `assets` chain on the cells' version, skips every step that needs a pushed tag, signing or publishing, and still checks the `release-assets` paths. No asset is ever replaced once uploaded: a rerun skips identical assets and fails on a different one.
- `release-consumer.yml`: runs when a release is published, or by dispatch with a `tag`. On the five release platforms it builds the quickstart consumer against the published source archive and checks that `@rules_dx//:dx` is the prebuilt download and prints the released version, that topiary and progenitor are the prebuilt downloads, that `@rules_dx//config:tool_govet` is the prebuilt dx-go and `tool_modfmt` runs, on Linux that kcov is the prebuilt download, and on `windows-arm64` that the `pkl_lsp` natives jar packs the prebuilt tree-sitter and tree-sitter-pkl DLLs. It skips releases whose tag does not start with `v`, such as `mirror-php-<version>`. When every `consumer` job is green, its `bcr` job calls `bazel-contrib/publish-to-bcr` (pinned v1.7.0) to open the BCR pull request from the `BCR_REGISTRY_FORK` fork with `BCR_PUBLISH_TOKEN`; it is skipped while that variable is unset and for `v0.0.*` tags. Its `bcr-ledger` job runs `//deploy/private/release:bcr_ledger` and records the pull request URL, `failed`, or `not-authorized` for a skipped `bcr` job, in the run summary and the `bcr-ledger` artifact.
- `upgrade-e2e.yml`: when a release is published, or by dispatch with optional `from` and `to`. Runs `producers_bin --upgrade-e2e`: a throwaway consumer on the second-latest BCR release runs `dx init`, upgrades to the latest and back with `dx upgrade --to <version> --apply`, and runs `bazel test //...` after each step. It needs two published releases on the BCR. `producers_bin --upgrade-e2e --from <from> --to local` upgrades to this checkout instead (`local_path_override` at the root `MODULE.bazel` version), so the run uses the tree's own dx. After `dx init` and each upgrade it reads `bazel mod graph --output=json` and fails when the consumer names `rules_php`, `rules_lua` or `rules_qt`, when a rule set does not resolve to exactly the floor of the target rules_dx release, or when rules_dx does not resolve to the target version.

## Main health

`ci.yml` runs only on `workflow_dispatch`, a daily schedule (`17 3 * * *`, UTC) against the default branch head, and `merge_group`. There are no push or pull-request triggers. Its `gate` job (`statuses: read`) first fails a merge group whose pull request head has a pending, failed or errored `evidence/*` status, then runs `dx check --affected`, checks `MODULE.bazel.lock` is current and checks that its per-platform go_sdk and python entries agree. `.github/rulesets/main.json` requires `gate` and `pr-links` on main. Runs share one concurrency group per ref (`ci-ci-<ref>`, no cancel): a new run on main replaces only the queued one. The repository cache prune runs after scheduled or dispatched main runs. A red scheduled run opens or updates one issue titled `ci: scheduled run is failing` (the `scheduled-report` job). The next green scheduled run closes it. After each scheduled or dispatched run on main, the same job rewrites the pinned issue labelled `known-red` with the test labels that failed in that run. GitHub may delay or drop scheduled runs under load.

The platform table is `PLATFORMS` in `tools/ci/input_validation/src/lib.rs`; `input_validation_test` pins every other copy to it.

Land a PR with `gh pr checks <n> --watch --fail-fast --required`, then `gh pr merge <n> --squash`, never `--admin`.

The consumer contract is [GitHub CI](../../docs/github-ci.md).
